full_judgment:
8. Mr Chakraborty, in the course of argument after placing the impugned order and other materials on record submits that the application for substitution filed by the plaintiff, in fact, was not in form inasmuch as the plaintiff without disclosing the exact date of the death of deceased defendants in a cursory manner stated that the defendant Nos. 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 14 and 20 died and for which the heirs of the deceased needs to be substituted. Mr Chakraborty, further points out that the application for substitution is also heavily barred by limitation in view of the provisions of Article 177 of the Limitation Act but the learned trial Judge without considering all these legal aspects of the case abruptly allowed the application for substitution by Order No. 10 dated 15-6-2008 which resulted in the failure of justice and, as such,, the impugned order is laible to be set-aside. 

 13. Mr Chakraborty, seriously assailed the impugned order in submitting that the learned trial Judge without assigning any reason whatsoever, allowed the application for substitution in a summary manner giving a go-by to the materials aspects of the case as like as the plaintiff did not mention the date of death of deceased-defendants in the application as well as the application for substitution was heavily barred by limitation. 

 16. In the case of Md Matiur Rahman vs Lalbanu Bibi reported in 6 BLD 432, if has been held that an application for substitution filed beyond the period of limitation without seeking for an order setting aside abatement shall be treated as an application for setting aside abatement and for substitution of the legal hears.
